# Developing and Benchmarking Verification Algorithms to Improve Text-to-SQL Generation

[All reading notes](../reading-notes.md) · [Catalog entry](../README.md#verification-algorithms)

**Full paper read · 2026-11-09**

[Original source](https://www.vldb.org/pvldb/vol19/p3732-alrashed.pdf) · PVLDB 19(11), pp. 3732-3744, 2026

**Reading coverage:** All 13 pages, Sections 1-9, Tables 1-8, figures and captions; rendered Table 7/Practical Utility checked. No appendices in the proceedings PDF.

## Research question

Syntactically valid SQL may silently misrepresent a request, while reference-based execution labels can themselves be wrong.

## Method

Round-trip critique translates SQL back to language before judging intent alignment. Synthetic execution creates small databases and expected answers, then compares candidate execution. Boolean combinations trade false acceptance against false rejection; accepted candidates form a selective generator.

## Evaluation

Gemini-2.5-Pro is held fixed across methods on Spider, BIRD and KaggleDBQA candidates. Execution-based labels provide the main oracle; 90 verifier-selected cases receive manual audit. Accuracy, coverage, latency and penalty-dependent utility are reported.

## What the results support

Conservative combinations reject more erroneous candidates at substantial coverage and inference-cost penalties. The manual audit finds genuine reference errors and ambiguity, as well as synthetic-data and answer-generation failures.

## Limits and qualifications

Audited subsets are selected by verifier behavior, so their error fractions are not global benchmark prevalence. Synthetic tests are finite and model-generated, not semantic proofs. Reported false-rejection and benchmark-cleaning estimates contain table/prose and arithmetic conflicts; quoted deployment-safety claims should therefore remain qualified.

## Relevance to reliable Text-to-SQL

Useful reference-free verification and abstention design, with explicit distinctions between candidate failure, input ambiguity and benchmark noise.
